items.title: SenseTime launches RiRiXin SenseNova 6.8 Flash, adds dynamic PPT and 3D design support

extra.hover: 【SenseTime launches RiRiXin SenseNova 6.8 Flash, adds dynamic PPT and 3D design support】Nov. 3 — SenseTime released the RiRiXin SenseNova 6.8 Flash official version, targeting office collaboration and design-generation workflows. The update adds long-term memory and cross-session task collaboration; design outputs now cover dynamic PPT, animated posters, web and SVG assets, and Blender 3D creation, with integration hooks for Figma. The model is available for online demo and a SenseNova Token Plan went live simultaneously.

items.title: RESERVE BANK OF AUSTRALIA hikes for fifth time this year; elevated inflation extends tightening cycle

extra.hover: 【RESERVE BANK OF AUSTRALIA hikes for fifth time this year; elevated inflation extends tightening cycle】The RESERVE BANK OF AUSTRALIA voted 6-3 to raise the cash rate 25bps to 4.85%, the highest level since 2008 and the central bank's fifth hike in 2026. Three board members dissented and the bank gave no clear signal on further tightening. The RBA materially raised its inflation profile, projecting headline CPI to peak at 4.5% in Q4 and both headline and trimmed-mean inflation to remain above 3% through end-2027—about three quarters later than its August forecast. Inflation is now projected to return to the 2.5% midpoint target only by mid-2028. The bank cited higher fuel and commodity prices from the Middle East conflict, stronger-than-expected domestic capacity pressure, and AI-driven demand for tech goods as key upward drivers.

items.title: Australia treasurer: RBA hike expected; households and firms remain under pressure, government to seek spending savings

extra.hover: 【Australia treasurer: RBA hike expected; households and firms remain under pressure, government to seek spending savings】Treasurer Jim Chalmers said the RBA's rate rise was already priced in by markets but will not ease pressure on Australian households and businesses. He said many Australians are paying a heavy price for external factors beyond their control. The government will take responsibility for fighting inflation; while rolling out targeted relief measures it will also look for ways to reduce spending.

items.title: Joe Tsai urges model open-sourcing; Alibaba says Qianwen >470 open models, 4 bln downloads

extra.hover: 【Joe Tsai urges model open-sourcing; Alibaba says Qianwen >470 open models, 4 bln downloads】At the World Internet Conference Wuzhen Summit on the morning of Nov. 3, Alibaba Group co-founder and chairman Joe Tsai said AI demand continues to climb and Chinese firms are accelerating model open-sourcing and ecosystem openness, with key metrics such as open-model downloads remaining market-leading. He said only open source can drive widespread adoption and enable a sustainable, inclusive era of intelligence. Tsai noted Alibaba proposed an open-source strategy three years ago; Alibaba Qianwen has open-sourced more than 470 models and cumulative global downloads have topped 4 billion.

items.title: RBA hikes in split vote; cash rate at 18-year high

extra.hover: 【RBA hikes in split vote; cash rate at 18-year high】The Reserve Bank of Australia on Tuesday raised the cash rate 25bps to 4.85%, an 18-year high and the fifth hike this year, extending one of the most aggressive tightening cycles among developed economies. The nine-member rate-setting board approved the move in a 6-3 split. In its statement the RBA said the committee will continue to take the measures it judges necessary to ensure inflation returns sustainably to target. Governor Bullock will hold a press conference at 3:30pm Sydney time and is expected to be asked about the likelihood of further hikes amid persistent inflation, global energy shocks and domestic capacity constraints.

items.title: China A-shares midday: major indices trade lower in wide swings; AI compute-hardware leads declines

extra.hover: 【China A-shares midday: major indices trade lower in wide swings; AI compute-hardware leads declines】China A-shares traded in a wide range below the prior close at midday after early volatility: ChiNext (创业板指) dropped over 2% on the open, briefly turned positive, then weakened again; the STAR 50 index fell more than 3% intraday. At the midday close Shanghai Composite -0.71%, Shenzhen Composite -0.16%, ChiNext -0.94%. Turnover on the two exchanges exceeded 9.0 trillion yuan and more than 3,300 stocks were up. Sector moves: cinema chains and cultural media extended gains; gaming and pork were among top advancers and batteries remained active. AI compute-hardware, CPO and storage chips showed weakness; oil shipping and innovative drugs were notably under pressure.
